domain.name: inv_single
domain.one_line: Single-echelon periodic-review inventory with stochastic lead time and backlogging.

demand.domain: real, [0, inf); independent across periods given the period's distribution, which may itself carry a per-episode latent
demand.source: single-item periodic-review inventory control (Scarf 1960; Zipkin 2000 ch. 6, 9): demand is the exogenous driver

leadtime.source: the theory admits a random replenishment lead time; a scenario selecting a point mass is a design choice, not a scope reduction

order.source: the control: a non-negative replenishment quantity placed once per period, with no capacity limit in the theory

inventory.domain: real; unbounded below when unmet demand is backlogged, non-negative when it is lost
inventory.source: on-hand stock less backorders, the level the holding and shortage costs are charged on

T.source: finite planning horizon, with no salvage value or terminal cost at the end

h.source: holding cost per unit of positive end-of-period stock, per period

b.source: shortage cost per unit short, charged per period while backlogged and once per unit when lost

K.source: fixed cost charged whenever an order is placed; K > 0 is what makes the optimal policy (s,S) rather than order-up-to (Scarf 1960)

out_of_scope: capacity limits on the order quantity: the theory admits any non-negative order, so the rendering's upper bound is a design cap and never a physical one
supplier reliability and partial delivery: an order once placed always arrives in full
perishability, obsolescence and any age-dependent stock value
salvage value or terminal cost at the horizon end
pricing, demand shaping and substitution: the order quantity is the only control
multi-item and multi-echelon coupling: one item, one stocking point
dynamics: each period runs three events in a declared order: place an order, receive arrivals, realize demand

an order placed in period t arrives at the start of period t + L, where L is that period's realized lead time; when L is random orders may cross, so the outstanding quantity is not summarized by its total alone
forall k in 1..pipeline_len-1: outstanding[k] <- outstanding[k+1] each period, with the newly placed order entering the slot its realized lead time selects
inventory[t+1] = inventory[t] + arrivals[t] - demand[t] when unmet demand is backlogged; inventory[t+1] = max(inventory[t] + arrivals[t] - demand[t], 0) when it is lost
cost[t] = h * max(inventory[t], 0) + b * max(-inventory[t], 0) + K * indicator(order[t] > 0) + c * order[t]
minimize the expected undiscounted sum of cost[t] over t in 0..T-1

notation.x: inventory position = inventory + total outstanding orders
notation.S: order-up-to level of a base-stock policy, optimal when K = 0
notation.s: reorder point; with S it gives the (s,S) policy Scarf 1960 proves optimal when K > 0

state_variables.name: period
state_variables.desc: current period t; horizon ends when period == T

state_variables.name: inventory

narrowed.to: integer lattice, bounded to +/- inv_bound_mult * demand.mean
narrowed.by: selection:every shipped demand candidate is integer-valued + implementation:a finite box is needed for a static observation space

state_variables.desc: net on-hand inventory after all period events; read by next transition

state_variables.name: pipeline

narrowed.to: a fixed-length vector of pipeline_len slots, so lead times above pipeline_len - 1 cannot be represented
narrowed.by: implementation:the state must have a static shape; pipeline_len is an axis-tagged design constant resolved per instance, so the width follows the sweep rather than capping it

state_variables.desc: pipeline[k] = quantity arriving at the k-th future R (receive) event; read by next R

placement.rationale: no later transition reads it and no observation mode exposes it: `demand` is diagnostic-only, carried for eval and probe readouts

info_fields.name: leadtime
info_fields.desc: sampled lead time of this period's order

info_fields.name: action_period
info_fields.desc: period the emitting decision was taken (boundary invariant)

decisions.name: order

type.rationale: the problem statement imposes no integrality on 'how much to order', so the THEORY admits any non-negative quantity. The integer lattice the default rendering places orders on is a design choice, not a fact about inventory control -- recorded in `narrowed`, not here. (The earlier rationale argued 'continuous is easier for PPO', which is a rendering-level claim in a theory-level field, and a falsified one.)

bounds.rationale: order_cap_mult x mean demand; upper bound caps the action scale, not a physical limit. Symbolic so each demand candidate resizes to its own scale.

narrowed.to: integer lattice on [0, floor(2 * demand.max() * max(1, leadtime.max()))] -- e.g. Discrete(46) at simple, Discrete(91) at lt
narrowed.by: design:the default action mode is order_discrete, because the order flows into integer stock (#E4 found the inherited continuous encoding accounted for the whole of the simple gap) + implementation:the upper bound is an action-scale cap, not a physical limit the theory states -- and it is the GYM's own cap (2 x demand.max() x max(1, leadtime.max()), in _build_action_space), which is tighter than and independent of this decision's declared bound order_cap_mult * demand.mean. #E2 measured what that costs: the optimal policy's largest order over 512 episodes is 23 (simple), 37 (simple_k and lt), 48 (slt) against caps of 45/45/91/136, so 0 of 15360 actions per scenario are cut off. order_cap_mult therefore names the DECLARED bound only -- nothing in the gym reads it

decisions.desc: replenishment quantity placed at the O (order) event

updates: if stockout_mode == 'lost_sales': lost_sales = max(0, -inventory); inventory = max(0, inventory)

per_step_components.name: holding
per_step_components.desc: evaluated at END_OF_PERIOD on end-of-period inventory

per_step_components.name: shortage
per_step_components.expr: b * max(0, -inventory) if stockout_mode == 'backlog' else b * lost_sales
per_step_components.desc: evaluated at END_OF_PERIOD: on end-of-period backlog, or on this period's lost sales in the lost-sales variant

invariants.name: inventory_balance
invariants.desc: on-hand changes only by receipts and demand; under lost_sales the unmet part is recorded in lost_sales rather than carried as negative inventory, so the same balance holds in both stockout modes

invariants.name: pipeline_balance
invariants.desc: outstanding orders change only by what is placed and what arrives — holds under every event order and every lead-time candidate

invariants.name: lost_sales_only_in_lost_sales_mode
invariants.desc: backlog mode never records a lost sale

invariants.name: no_negative_stock_under_lost_sales
invariants.desc: lost-sales mode drops unmet demand instead of backlogging it

constants.name: horizon_T
constants.desc: planning horizon T (rendering choice; the theory says only 'integer >= 1'). Named so an instance can render the model at another horizon -- the L1 derivation is based at T~=30, so a longer-T instance owes a re-derivation, which the launch check will say

constants.name: order_cap_mult
constants.desc: order-cap multiplier: the action-scale cap is order_cap_mult * demand.mean (a design cap, never physical -- mdp.model declares order unbounded above). Named so the one coefficient has one home across the decision and both action modes

constants.name: inv_bound_mult
constants.desc: state-envelope multiplier: inventory in +/- inv_bound_mult * demand.mean, pipeline slots in [0, inv_bound_mult * demand.mean]. A finite box for a static observation space, not a model claim

constants.name: h
constants.desc: holding cost per unit of positive end-of-period stock

constants.name: b
constants.desc: shortage cost per unit of backlog

constants.name: K
constants.desc: fixed cost per order placed (0 in the simple base)

constants.name: c
constants.desc: variable cost per unit ordered (0 in the simple base: ordering is free)

constants.name: simple_rate
constants.desc: simple candidate: fixed Poisson demand rate (scenario_simple's Poisson(10))

constants.name: leadtime_value
constants.desc: deterministic candidate: fixed lead time (0 in the simple base; instances raise it)

constants.name: pipeline_len
constants.desc: pipeline vector length = max lead time + 1 for the active leadtime candidate; per-instance (base det-0 -> 1, lt-2 -> 3, slt{2..5} -> 6)

constants.name: stockout_mode
constants.desc: unmet-demand handling (categorical): 'backlog' = accumulates as negative inventory; 'lost_sales' = dropped each period. Read by the D-event update and the shortage objective; mirrors InvSingleScenario.stockout_mode.

constants.name: event_order
constants.desc: within-period event order: a permutation of O (place order), R (receive), D (demand), with R before D. Named constant in control position (§10d) so instances select an order variant and the interpreter runs transitions in the resolved order; the 'R','O','D' order needs leadtime.min() >= 1.

constants.name: demand_support_size
constants.desc: discrete candidate: number of support points in the per-episode demand distribution

constants.name: demand_support_low
constants.desc: discrete candidate: lowest integer the per-episode support is drawn from

constants.name: demand_support_high
constants.desc: discrete candidate: highest integer the per-episode support is drawn from

constants.name: demand_alpha
constants.desc: poisson candidate: Gamma shape of the hidden Poisson rate; E[lambda] = alpha/beta = 30

constants.name: demand_beta
constants.desc: poisson candidate: Gamma rate of the hidden Poisson rate; sd[lambda] = sqrt(alpha)/beta = 10

mixtures.name: mix_demand
mixtures.desc: nature's 50/50 pick of the demand regime per episode: the discrete instance vs the poisson instance (both on slt lead, pipeline_len 6) — a cross-family mixture; the component's own selection applies for its episodes (standalone equivalence)

simple.desc: fixed-rate Poisson demand (rate=demand_rate); the scenario_simple base — non-latent

discrete.desc: per-episode discrete demand distribution: a support of demand_support_size integers drawn without replacement from [demand_support_low, demand_support_high] with normalized-uniform weights (hidden world latent)

poisson.desc: Poisson demand with hidden per-episode rate lambda ~ Gamma(demand_alpha, demand_beta) (shape-rate; the conjugate prior for a Poisson rate)

deterministic.desc: fixed lead time (value=leadtime_value); the scenario_simple base

slt.desc: stochastic lead time on a fixed discrete support {1,2,3}, uniform -- E[L]=2 matches the deterministic lt instance, so lt -> slt varies lead-time variability (and order crossover) at a matched mean

observation_modes.name: vec_ctx
observation_modes.desc: `vec` plus the cost regime (critical fractile b/(b+h), fixed cost K): what a generalist over the `grid16` / `cost_leadtime` cost x lead-time grids conditions on. Carries no lead-time law -- those grids vary the lead time through the pipeline width, not through a law.

observation_modes.name: vec_ctx_slt
observation_modes.desc: `vec_ctx` plus the LEAD-TIME LAW in force -- `leadtime.probs`, folded at load from the selected candidate (upstream #77, v0.10.7), never the constant that parameterises one candidate. `dim: 3` is the categorical candidate's support {1,2,3}: the `lt_variance_*` grids sweep the law on that support and a generalist over them must see which law it faces. Under the deterministic candidate the law folds to the one-point pmf (width 1), so the gym refuses the mode by width rather than by family -- the narrowing is the declared width, not a code-side rule.

observation_modes.name: vec_ip_ctx_slt
observation_modes.desc: `vec_ip` plus exactly the context `vec_ctx_slt` carries (law, fractile, K): the restricted-information control for the `lt_variance_*` generalist. Same `dim: 3` law, same width rule.

action_modes.name: order_discrete
action_modes.desc: identity encoding over integral order quantities. The default because the order flows into integer stock (`inventory: int`, `pipeline: int_vector`), so a fractional order would put non-integers into an integer state; the gym derives it from `demand.is_discrete` (action_mode='auto'). A categorical head also removes the action-scale hazard the continuous mode carries — see #E4 in the pre-restart log (`git show 27e0546:inv_single/ESCALATION.md`)

action_modes.name: order
action_modes.desc: identity: the agent emits the order quantity directly, clipped into bounds

action_modes.name: order_hurdle
action_modes.desc: two-part (hurdle) encoding: MultiDiscrete([2, q_high]) whose first head decides WHETHER to order and whose second decides HOW MANY units in [1, q_high]. It reaches exactly the same order quantities as `order_discrete`, so on a categorical head it is near-equivalent by construction — the atom at zero is already its own action there. It exists to ISOLATE the quantity head, so an ordinal or zero-inflated parameterization can be swapped in without also moving the order/do-not-order decision (README.md, `3-methodology` Q-B)

reward_modes.name: neg_cost
reward_modes.desc: negated per-step cost.total (sense=minimize, reward is maximized)

requires_memory.rationale: hidden world latent (per-episode demand distribution) suggests memory; overridden to reactive for the baseline pipeline

obs_normalization.rationale: inventory and pipeline entries are stationary features of heterogeneous magnitude (scale set by the selected demand candidate); spec §8.3 says normalize

benchmarks.name: dp
benchmarks.basis: Backward induction over the discretized state with the order grid enumerated per state; the DP state is inventory at LT=0 and inventory position at LT>=1. EXACT for the discretized MDP under backlog, both at LT=0 and at any DETERMINISTIC LT>=1 -- the LT>1 case verified against an independently derived exact DP over the full pipeline state (`inv_single_dp_exactness.py`, campaign item A7a), which reduces (inv, p0, p1) to (inv + p0, p1) and agrees on every action in every period at `lt`. NOT exact on two instance families, where this role does not hold and `mdp_gates --ir` must not be pointed at it: under stochastic lead time (`slt`) orders can cross, so inventory position is not a sufficient statistic and the table is only a heuristic; under lost sales (`lost_sales`, `discrete_lost_sales`, `poisson_lost_sales`, `lt_lost_sales`) the cost recursion is backlog-only, so THIS table is not a valid bar at all -- but that is a statement about this implementation, not about the problem: `dp_lostsales` below solves the lost-sales case exactly at deterministic LT and IS the bar there.

benchmarks.name: dp_lostsales
benchmarks.basis: Backward induction for the LOST-SALES instances at DETERMINISTIC lead time, where the shipped `dp` is invalid. Under event order O-R-D the receipt lands before demand, so `inv` and `p0` enter only through `u = inv + p0`; the next period is `u' = (u-d)^+ + p1`, whose truncation at zero is NOT linear in `u`, so `u` and `p1` cannot collapse further into inventory position -- the exact recursion is two-dimensional, `V_t(u, p1)`. This is why base-stock is not optimal here (Karlin & Scarf 1958) and why the backlog table does not apply. `(u, p1)` is the STANDARD lost-sales state, not a reduction below it: the classical formulation is on-hand after receipt plus the L-1 outstanding orders, dimension L, which at L=2 is two. This DP is cheap because this domain's L is 2. EXACT for the discretized MDP at any deterministic LT under lost sales; NOT valid under stochastic lead time (`slt`, and the latent-demand `*_lost_sales` instances, which also carry a per-episode demand law this table does not condition on). Verified two independent ways in `inv_single_benchmark_dp_lostsales.py`: against the un-reduced 3-D DP over `(inv, p0, p1)` (max gap 6e-14), and by simulating its own policy through `InvSingleEnv` over the 8192-seed protocol block (415.79 vs analytic V_0 415.65, +0.19 SE). At `lt_lost_sales` the optimum is 415.79 and the best fitted base-stock costs 451.82, so 36.02 -- 8.66% -- is the structural gap base-stock leaves under lost sales.

benchmarks.name: heuristic
benchmarks.basis: Ordering rules run through `InvSingleEnv` under the real information set, one file with `--policy` selecting among them (spec 9.8). `myopic` orders up to the newsvendor fractile of demand over the protection interval L+1, measured on inventory position; `basestock` orders up to a fixed S on inventory position, with `--optimize` grid-searching S by simulation on the SELECTION seed block, never the reporting block. `capped_basestock` is Xin (2021)'s two-parameter family `q = min(cap, (S-IP)+)`, whose limits are pure base-stock (cap -> inf) and pure constant-order (S -> inf); `--optimize` grid-searches the PAIR on the selection block, which matters because the two levers substitute. It is the shape the exact lost-sales DP takes at `lt_lost_sales`, worth 33 cost units there over uncapped base-stock -- 91.7% of the gap base-stock leaves (#E17). `constant` orders the demand mean every period. `zero` and `random` are the do-nothing and did-it-learn-anything floors that spec 8.6 makes a build diagnosis rather than an escalation trigger.

benchmarks.name: weighted
benchmarks.basis: Order-up-to on a WEIGHTED inventory position: q = max(0, S - (inv + sum_k w_k*pipe_k)). Generalizes the `heuristic` benchmark's `basestock` policy, which is exactly the w=(1,1,...,1) member -- at all-ones the search returns the same S* and the same reported cost to the cent, so the two are not independent implementations and may be compared paired. S is grid-searched on the SELECTION seed block by the same protocol as `--optimize`, never the reporting block. Motivated by `slt`, where order crossover makes unweighted inventory position insufficient (campaign #E12) and a single discount on the farthest pipeline slot recovers about half the gap to the trained policy (#E13); w may be supplied (`--mode net`, e.g. read out of a distilled policy) or fitted by cost (`--mode search`). At w=(1,1,...,1) this is the textbook rule the order-crossover literature uses, which corrects only S and leaves the weights at one.

tier2.structure: order-up-to / (s,S) threshold structure on inventory position
tier2.claim: the trained policy is order-up-to at K=0 and (s,S) at K>0, recovering the thresholds the exact DP computes rather than merely matching its cost
tier2.instrument: inv_single_policy_probe.py — action-surface sweep over inventory x period, structural-form fit, action agreement against the DP's (s_t, S_t), and paired scoring of the fitted rule replayed through the same gym

tier2.structure: inventory position as the sufficient statistic under deterministic lead time
tier2.claim: at `lt`, PPO on the raw state (`vec`) matches PPO on inventory position (`vec_ip`) — the net rebuilds the statistic, so the transform need not be handed over; at `slt`, where order crossing breaks sufficiency, `vec_ip` stops being enough and `vec` matches or beats it
tier2.instrument: paired obs-mode contrast (vec vs vec_ip) on shared CRN seed blocks at `lt` and `slt`; probe sensitivity to individual pipeline components, which should collapse onto their sum at `lt` and not at `slt`

tier2.structure: deviation from base-stock under lost sales with positive lead time
tier2.claim: at `lt_lost_sales` the learned policy beats the tuned base-stock heuristic, and its orders sit at-or-below the fitted base-stock rule's in high-stock states — the direction lost-sales theory predicts; `lost_sales` (LT=0) is the near-newsvendor control where base-stock should be unbeatable
tier2.instrument: probe action surface vs the fitted base-stock rule; paired scoring of both on the shared protocol block (no exact DP exists — the backlog recursion is not a valid bar here)

tier2.structure: optimal policy structure under stochastic lead time with potential order crossover
tier2.claim: at `slt` the learned policy on the full pipeline (`vec`) beats every rule measured on inventory position alone — optimized base-stock, myopic, and the backlog DP table run as a heuristic — and its action depends on pipeline composition at fixed inventory position, the signature of a crossover-aware rule
tier2.instrument: shares the slt arms with the sufficient-statistic question (`vec_ip` is the restricted-information control); probe the action surface across pipeline compositions at fixed IP; fit the best IP-only rule to the net and score the residual, paired

tier2.structure: the DP's (s,S) map as a function of (b, K, leadtime) across the grid16 cells
tier2.claim: one policy trained on grid16's sampler with the cost context observed (`vec_ctx`) tracks each cell's exact-DP cost; a context-blind `vec` arm prices what observing the regime is worth. NARROWED 2026-09-11 (see ESCALATION.md FRAME-CHANGELOG): the original claim also asserted THRESHOLD recovery and interpolation to interior fractiles. Thresholds were measured on the 8 LT=0 cells and confirmed there, but the probe holds the pipeline at zero, which is off-policy at LT>=1 and unreadable; interpolation is untestable on a grid whose train and eval cells are identical
tier2.instrument: per-cell paired scoring against each cell's exact DP, one leaderboard row per cell (spec 9.6). NO READBACK IS OWED (spec 14.0 probe_required): after the 2026-09-11 narrowing the surviving claim is an outcome comparison per cell, and the struck threshold clause is the one a readback would have served -- the probe holds the pipeline at zero, which is off-policy at LT>=1. Recorded here rather than in prose, per 14.0

tier2.structure: the DP's (s,S) map as a SMOOTH function of (b, K, leadtime): every column of the cost_leadtime bars is monotone in b with no violations, so a policy that learned the MAP rather than the sampled cells should realize it at regimes it never trained on
tier2.claim: the `vec_ctx` generalist trained on grid16's 16 cells tracks each HELD-OUT cell's exact-DP cost across cost_leadtime's 54 cells, with the 12 overlapping cells as the memorization control. Falsifiable form: %-of-optimal on held-out cells is not materially worse than on seen cells; a sharp drop means the policy fitted the 16 trained cells rather than the map. The two single-axis strata attribute any failure -- b-interpolation (24 cells, lead time held at a trained value) and leadtime-interpolation (6 cells, b held at a trained value). b in 5..8 INTERPOLATE, never extrapolate: b=19 stays in the training grid to anchor the top of the range. The context-blind `vec` arm cannot condition on the regime at all and is the lower control. NO THRESHOLD CLAUSE: the probe holds the pipeline at zero, which is off-policy at LT>=1, and RQ-6's threshold clause was struck for exactly that reason -- this question declares only what its instruments can read
tier2.instrument: per-cell paired scoring against each cell's exact DP, reported BY STRATUM -- seen (12) / b-interpolation only (24) / leadtime-interpolation only (6) / both (12); one leaderboard row per cell (spec 9.6). NO NEW TRAINING: the artifact is #E23's tuned grid16 generalist. NO READBACK IS OWED (spec 14.0 probe_required): the claim is a per-stratum cost comparison against each cell's exact DP and declares no structural readback, deliberately -- no policy was trained for this question, so there is no new artifact to read back

grids.name: grid16
grids.desc: RQ-6 generality target: shortage cost b (critical fractile 0.5/0.8/0.9/0.95) x fixed cost K (base-stock vs (s,S) regime) x deterministic lead time, crossed on `lt` so every cell keeps pipeline_len=3 — the family maximum, the spec-5.6 padding obligation for one policy across LT 0 and 2. All cells backlog + deterministic LT, so the dp benchmark's `exact` role holds at every cell. Cells (b=9,K=0,LT=0), (b=9,K=20,LT=0), (b=9,K=0,LT=2) coincide with the `simple`, `simple_k`, `lt` specialist targets.

grids.name: cost_leadtime
grids.desc: RQ-7 interpolation target: the SAME family as `grid16` at finer resolution -- shortage cost b x fixed cost K x deterministic lead time, 54 cells, crossed on `lt` so `lt_max` is 2 and every cell keeps pipeline_len=3, IDENTICAL to grid16's. That is what lets one policy trained on grid16's sampler be scored here without the observation width changing. `grid16` is the TRAINING grid and this is the EVALUATION grid; their cell ids share a format, so the 12 overlapping cells (b in {1,4,9} x K x leadtime_value in {0,2}) are bit-identical and act as the memorization control. The 42 held-out cells fall in three strata that separate the axes: b-interpolation only (b in {2,3,5,6,7,8}, leadtime_value in {0,2}, 24 cells); leadtime-interpolation only (b in {1,4,9}, leadtime_value=1, 6 cells); and both (12 cells). grid16's b=19 column is deliberately OUTSIDE this grid -- it anchors the top of the training range so b in 5..8 INTERPOLATE rather than extrapolate. All cells backlog + deterministic LT, so the dp benchmark's `exact` role holds at every one and every held-out cell has a verified bar.

grids.name: lt_variance_k0
grids.desc: RQ-4 generality target: does ONE linear statistic of (inventory, pipeline) serve a whole family, or must its weights move with the cell? Two axes. (1) Lead-time VARIABILITY at MATCHED MEAN -- probs [p, 1-2p, p] on support {1,2,3}, so E[L]=2 at every cell while Var(L)=2p spans its full admissible range: p in {0, 1/6, 1/4, 1/3, 1/2} gives Var 0, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 1. p<=1/2 is forced -- beyond it 1-2p is a negative probability -- so both ends are the family's own extremes. p=0 is degenerate at L=2 and reproduces the `lt` dynamics; p=1/3 is uniform and reproduces `slt`; both are already measured (#E13: far-slot weight 1.00 and ~0.70), so the sweep is bracketed with a measured interior point. p=1/2 is the maximum-variance endpoint and is BIMODAL -- all mass on {1,3}, none on the mean itself -- so a jump there is not evidence about variance alone. (2) Shortage cost b uniform on the integers 1..9, i.e. critical fractile b/(b+1) from 0.50 to 0.90; the grid sampler draws cells with equal weight, so training sees b uniform while evaluation still enumerates 9 discrete cells with per-cell leaderboards. Lead-time LENGTH is held fixed: changing E[L] moves the order-up-to level and the whole cost scale, which would confound the weight question. Every cell keeps support {1,2,3} hence pipeline_len=4, so the observation vector never changes shape and one policy spans the grid without padding. Base is `slt`, which selects a non-default candidate: expressible only from v0.10.2 (issue #75). K IS NOT AN AXIS HERE: K=0 and K>0 are different policy STRUCTURES (order-up-to vs (s,S)), so one generalist spanning both would have to switch structure mid-family and a cross-K comparison would be meaningless. They are two grids, two generalists, two leaderboards -- the same rule that makes every scenario a separate leaderboard. This grid fixes K=0: no fixed order cost, so base-stock is the optimal structure.

grids.name: lt_variance_k20
grids.desc: RQ-4 generality target: does ONE linear statistic of (inventory, pipeline) serve a whole family, or must its weights move with the cell? Two axes. (1) Lead-time VARIABILITY at MATCHED MEAN -- probs [p, 1-2p, p] on support {1,2,3}, so E[L]=2 at every cell while Var(L)=2p spans its full admissible range: p in {0, 1/6, 1/4, 1/3, 1/2} gives Var 0, 1/3, 1/2, 2/3, 1. p<=1/2 is forced -- beyond it 1-2p is a negative probability -- so both ends are the family's own extremes. p=0 is degenerate at L=2 and reproduces the `lt` dynamics; p=1/3 is uniform and reproduces `slt`; both are already measured (#E13: far-slot weight 1.00 and ~0.70), so the sweep is bracketed with a measured interior point. p=1/2 is the maximum-variance endpoint and is BIMODAL -- all mass on {1,3}, none on the mean itself -- so a jump there is not evidence about variance alone. (2) Shortage cost b uniform on the integers 1..9, i.e. critical fractile b/(b+1) from 0.50 to 0.90; the grid sampler draws cells with equal weight, so training sees b uniform while evaluation still enumerates 9 discrete cells with per-cell leaderboards. Lead-time LENGTH is held fixed: changing E[L] moves the order-up-to level and the whole cost scale, which would confound the weight question. Every cell keeps support {1,2,3} hence pipeline_len=4, so the observation vector never changes shape and one policy spans the grid without padding. Base is `slt`, which selects a non-default candidate: expressible only from v0.10.2 (issue #75). K IS NOT AN AXIS HERE: K=0 and K>0 are different policy STRUCTURES (order-up-to vs (s,S)), so one generalist spanning both would have to switch structure mid-family and a cross-K comparison would be meaningless. They are two grids, two generalists, two leaderboards -- the same rule that makes every scenario a separate leaderboard. This grid fixes K=20 -- the same fixed cost `simple_k` and `grid16` use, so the regime is comparable with the rest of the campaign rather than a new value: a fixed order cost, so (s,S) is the optimal structure and the policy must learn a trigger as well as a level.

assumptions_log: Order quantity modeled as continuous (float) and clipped to [0, 20*demand.mean]; the source description said 'how much to order' without specifying integrality.
Initial inventory and pipeline assumed empty (0).

Unmet demand is backlogged (stockout_mode='backlog'); the lost-sales variant is the 'lost_sales' scenario instance (stockout_mode='lost_sales'). Event order is the `event_order` constant (default O,R,D); the 'rdo' and 'rod' instances select R,D,O and R,O,D (§10d event-order-as-mode).
Cost components are evaluated at END_OF_PERIOD on end-of-period inventory.

`demand` placed in info (not state): no later transition reads it and no observation mode exposes it -- it is diagnostic-only, carried for eval and probe readouts. A variable no transition reads carries no information the policy can act on.
Period indexing is 0-based; horizon T=30; reaching T is `terminated` (T is part of the problem, no bootstrapping past it), not `truncated`.

DEMAND CANDIDATES (catalog): 'discrete' (default) draws a hidden per-episode 3-point distribution; 'poisson' draws a hidden per-episode rate lambda ~ Gamma(9, 0.3). Selected per instance ('poisson', 'poisson_lost_sales') or via --select demand=poisson; scale-derived bounds resolve per selection from the derived demand.mean (10 vs 30).

Seed scheme v2 (spec §6.3): intrinsic draws key [period, slot_stream_id, 1, episode_seed, seed_salt]; each slot's world latents draw on the meta branch at the SAME slot stream_id ([stream_id, 0, episode_seed, seed_salt]), so instances sharing a candidate share latent draws (common random numbers across instances).
